commitAtDiscovery: uncommitted working tree, branch phase-25-m2-verification (Phase 25 / DUR-05 DoD verification, after the real-YATA-port fix for R0010 and the sender-aware faultRelay.ts reorder fix)
oneLineDescription: The SAME R0010-class transitivity violation ('destIndex outside its own scan window') reproduces with ZERO duplicate delivery, ZERO reordering (not even the legal cross-sender kind), and ZERO drop -- pure, ordinary FIFO-per-sender delivery to 4 replicas is sufficient. The only 'fault' involved is completely unavoidable in any real distributed system: two different peers receiving the SAME broadcast message at different POINTS in their own respective local operation timelines, because real network latency to different peers is never identical. This is the minimal-precondition form of the R0010 finding -- it proves the underlying defect is not a fault-tolerance gap at all, but a correctness gap reachable under perfectly ordinary, non-adversarial concurrent editing at sufficient scale/replica count.
discoveryContext: Found while investigating a DUR-05 (Test Plan adverse-network DoD verification) finding: a real 4-client/2000-op run over faultRelay.ts (AFTER that file's own sender-aware-reorder fix, which closed the R0010-class same-sender-reordering gap) still showed a real, converged-but-wrong final document (length 820 vs expected 810 in one run; a genuine two-character transposition consistently visible on one of four replicas in a smaller 500-op run). A network-free, sender-aware combined-fault fuzzer (mirroring the corrected relay's own rules: reorder restricted to cross-sender only) found the SAME canary at 4 replicas under duplicate+delay+legal-reorder. Testing whether reorder was even necessary, a SECOND search with reorder forced to exactly 0 (pure duplicate+delay only) ALSO reproduced it. Delta-debugging the resulting minimal script (following R0008/R0009/R0010's own methodology) removed every duplicate-delivery event during minimization -- the final, fully-minimized 22-event repro contains no duplicated delivery, no reordered delivery, and no dropped delivery at all: every message is delivered to every recipient AT MOST ONCE, in an order consistent with a real network where DIFFERENT PEERS simply receive the SAME broadcast at different times relative to their own local activity.
harness: Same network-free event-script fuzzer/minimizer as R0010 (packages/engine/src/_dup1.test.ts/_dup2.test.ts/_dup3.test.ts, scratch, deleted after use), extended with sender-tracking so the reorder mechanic could be restricted to cross-sender-only (matching the corrected faultRelay.ts exactly) -- then re-run with reorderRate forced to 0 to test whether reorder was even a necessary ingredient. It was not.

minimalReproduction.description: 4 replicas (engine ids 1-4). 15 real operations, delivered via applyRemote in the listed order. Every delivery is to a DIFFERENT recipient than any prior delivery of that SAME message -- no duplicate delivery anywhere in this script. msg14 (the 15th operation, minted by replica0/engine id 1) throws while integrating on replica3/engine id 4.

replica3 (own mint): [c(tomb), i, d, h, a]
replica3 (own mint, fast path): [c(tomb), i, d, h, j, a]

timeline.note: replica0 receives 'g' IMMEDIATELY -- this is the ONLY delivery of msg6 to replica0; replica0 never sees anything else compete with 'g' before minting msg14 below.

DELAYED relative to replica0 -- delivered only now, AFTER replica3 has already independently built [c(tomb), i, d, h, j, a] from its OWN local activity in the meantime. Scanning [c(tomb),i,d,h,j,a] (whole document, oL=oR=null): 'g' ties-and-freezes against 'i' (Case-A-equivalent, same null origin, g would win a tie against i -- scanning=true, freezing destIndex at 1), then walks PAST d, h, j WITHOUT ever directly comparing against them (their own originLeft values don't match leftIndex=-1, so they don't reset `scanning`), finally reaching 'a' where the exact-origin-match-and-lose condition fires (a shares g's own (null,null) window exactly, and g does NOT win against a's own replica id) -- STOPS, with destIndex frozen at 1 (from the earlier freeze against 'i'). Final: replica3 = [c(tomb), g, i, d, h, j, a] -- g ends up BEFORE d, h, j, i, entirely because of WHEN it arrived relative to replica3's own unrelated local edits, never because of any direct comparison against any of them.

timeline.note: originLeft=d's id, originRight=g's id -- ON REPLICA0's OWN VIEW, d is strictly before g.

ready(): both d and g present on replica3 -> ready. integrate(): leftIndex = index(d) = 4 (replica3's structure is now [c(tomb)@0, g@1, i@2, d@3, h@4, j@5, a@6] -- wait, recompute exact positions from the trace: d ends up at index 4 in the 7-node structure once i is inserted before it). rightIndex = index(g) = 1. leftIndex+1(5) > rightIndex(1) -- INVERTED WINDOW. The scan loop's own `for(;;)` condition `i === rightIndex` is checked against i starting at leftIndex+1=5, which is already past rightIndex=1, so the loop body never runs even once. destIndex stays at its initial value, 5. Final check: destIndex(5) > rightIndex(1) -> THROWS.

minimalReproduction.exactError: integrate(): computed destIndex 5 for candidate 4:1 outside its own scan window [5, 1] — this is an integrate() bookkeeping bug in the real-YATA-ported algorithm (see the R0010 correction comment above) — please report as a new regression, do not assume it is R0008/R0009/R0010 recurring.

handTrace.summary: Identical mechanism to R0010 (transitivity of relative order across separate integrate() calls is not guaranteed by the real YATA algorithm's local, pairwise comparisons) but with a materially more severe precondition: R0010 required an explicit, artificial delivery-order violation (a message delivered to a receiver out of its own sender's send order, or a dropped-then-late-flushed message). This entry requires NEITHER. Every single delivery in this repro respects strict per-sender FIFO order, and no message is duplicated or dropped. The ONLY 'irregularity' is that msg6 ('g') reaches replica0 immediately but reaches replica3 only after replica3 has independently generated several of its OWN unrelated operations in the meantime -- i.e., ordinary, unavoidable network latency variance between two different point-to-point paths (server-to-replica0 vs server-to-replica3), which will always exist to SOME degree in any real deployment with more than a trivial number of concurrent users.
handTrace.whyNoFuzzConfigCaughtThis: None of this project's 7 convergence-fuzzer configs (C1-C7, 70,000+ seeds total, packages/testkit/src/fuzz/configs.ts) model this delivery pattern. C1-C6 ('deferred-shuffled') generate an entire trial's operations first, then deliver everything via ONE GLOBAL SHUFFLE at the very end -- every replica sees every operation at a shuffle-determined position in a SINGLE combined timeline, never 'this specific message reaches replica A immediately but reaches replica B only after several of B's own later, unrelated operations.' C7 ('immediate-delivery', added at R0008/R0009's own request specifically to close the gap C1-C6 had) broadcasts every operation to EVERY OTHER replica IMMEDIATELY and SYNCHRONOUSLY at mint time -- meaning by construction every replica receives a given message at (relatively) the same point in every OTHER replica's timeline too, since there is no delay differential at all. This repro's defining feature -- msg6 reaching replica0 immediately but reaching replica3 only after replica3's own subsequent, unrelated local mints -- is a THIRD, distinct delivery pattern (independent, per-TARGET delivery latency) that no existing fuzz config exercises. This is a genuine, load-bearing gap in this project's own primary correctness gate, of the same character as the 'deferred-shuffled cannot reach immediate-delivery bugs' gap Phase 20 already found and fixed by adding C7 -- except this time the missing pattern is 'independent per-target delay,' not 'immediate delivery' itself.
handTrace.confirmationOfSeverity: This is not a theoretical corner case requiring adversarial fault injection to reach. Any real deployment of this product with 3+ concurrent editors and ANY difference in network latency between different client connections (which is universal -- no two real network paths have identical latency) will, given enough concurrent editing volume, eventually reach the SAME precondition this repro constructs deliberately: a broadcast operation reaching different peers at meaningfully different points in each peer's own local edit timeline.

productionReachability: CONFIRMED via the real, end-to-end product stack, not just this network-free reduction: the originating finding (Test Plan DUR-05 DoD verification, Phase 25) reproduced first as a real 4-client/2000-operation session over a real WebSocket relay with only duplicate(5%)/delay(10%,1-3s)/reorder(10%, corrected to cross-sender-only) active, producing a converged-but-wrong document (length 820 vs expected 810); a smaller 500-operation run of the identical scenario showed a directly visible two-character transposition on one of four real, live SyncClient replicas. This engine-only fixture is the minimal, Rule-3-compliant reduction of that same underlying defect, now proven to need no fault injection (not even the legal, sender-aware kind) at all.
relatedEntriesNote: Same underlying algorithmic defect as R0010 (the real, published YATA algorithm's own transitivity gap, confirmed present in this project's port AND in production Yjs's own reference implementation, per the Phase 25 investigation's cross-check against https://github.com/yjs/yjs's actual Item.js source). This entry does not represent a new mechanism -- it represents the MINIMAL PRECONDITION under which R0010's mechanism is reachable: no fault injection of any kind, only ordinary per-target latency variance. Filed as a separate, permanent entry (not folded into R0010) specifically because the precondition difference is itself the load-bearing finding: it moves this defect from 'a fault-tolerance gap under adversarial conditions' to 'a correctness gap under ordinary concurrent use,' which changes how it must be prioritized and communicated.
status: OPEN. The standing R0010 fix (the real-YATA-port) and the standing faultRelay.ts sender-aware-reorder fix are BOTH confirmed correct and necessary as far as they go (they closed the specific mechanisms they targeted, verified via 70,000+ fuzz seeds, exhaustive R0008/R0009/R0010 delivery-order checks, and the full mutation matrix) -- neither is being reverted or questioned. This entry documents a THIRD, more fundamental precondition (no fault required) under which the SAME underlying algorithmic limitation surfaces, and identifies a genuine, load-bearing gap in this project's own convergence fuzz harness (no existing config models independent per-target delivery latency) as a necessary follow-up regardless of how the underlying algorithm defect itself is eventually addressed. DUR-06's own separate convergence-timing finding (from the same investigation) is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this entry and this session, per explicit user instruction to address it separately.
